judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Visible, required 'Nome*' field of #main-contact-form. It collects the user's own name (Input Purposes 'name'), and neither the input nor the form has an autocomplete attribute (checked in the snapshot and on the live page). Missing autocomplete on a user-information field is a standard 1.3.5 failure (H98 not met).

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Visible, required 'Cidade*' field of the contact form. It asks for the user's own city, which is the Input Purposes token 'address-level2'. There is no autocomplete attribute on the input or the form (confirmed live), so the purpose is not programmatically identified.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Visible, required 'E-mail*' field of the contact form. It collects the user's own email (Input Purposes 'email') and is type=text with no autocomplete attribute (confirmed live). This is a clear 1.3.5 failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Visible, required 'Telefone*' field of the contact form. It collects the user's own phone number (Input Purposes 'tel') and is type=text with no autocomplete attribute (confirmed live). The phone input mask does not identify the purpose.

judgments.rationale: #name in the newsletter form (#newsletter-form-f, yellow 'Assine nossa newsletter' band). It is visible, asks for the subscriber's own name (placeholder 'Informe seu nome', Input Purposes 'name') and has no autocomplete attribute (confirmed live). This is a 1.3.5 failure.

judgments.rationale: #email in the newsletter form. It is visible, asks for the subscriber's own email (placeholder 'E o seu email', Input Purposes 'email') and is type=text with no autocomplete attribute (confirmed live). This is a 1.3.5 failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The link text 'Clique aqui para iniciar uma conversa' states its purpose itself: start a conversation. Its context identifies who with: it follows the h1 'Sala de Imprensa (exclusivo para jornalistas)' and sits next to 'Contato: João (Pensata Assessoria)', his email and his phone number. A journalist can decide whether to follow it, so the claim that nothing around it explains it is factually wrong. The link does not name WhatsApp, and the WhatsApp icon has alt="", but 2.4.4 asks for the purpose, not the host. 'Clique aqui' wording and the unannounced new window are best-practice notes. The patch only rewords text that already meets the criterion.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The footer link 'Fatura Verde', under the h4 'Visite outros projetos', clearly names the project it is meant to open. The real defect is that /fatura-verde/ redirects to /404 'Página não encontrada' (confirmed live). A broken link affects every user the same way and is a content or QA bug, not a failure of 2.4.4, which is about whether the link's purpose can be determined from its text and context. The suggested text 'Fatura Verde (Página não encontrada)' is not a real accessibility fix; the fix is to repair or remove the link.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Under WCAG's definitions, a label is the text presented to all users, while a name may be exposed only to assistive technology. Here the visible label is the placeholder 'CPF*', which is descriptive. aria-label='document' is the accessible name, not the label. The real failure is 2.5.3 Label in Name: the visible text 'CPF' is not in the name 'document'. Placeholder-only labelling is also a 3.3.2 concern. Changing aria-label to 'CPF' fixes 2.5.3, not a 2.4.6 problem.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The visible label 'Telefone*' (placeholder) is descriptive. The accessible name 'phone' also clearly says what to enter, so the claim that it 'does not say what to enter' is wrong. The real issues are that the English name does not contain the visible Portuguese label (2.5.3 Label in Name) and has no lang marking. Neither is a 2.4.6 failure. The patch only translates text that already describes the purpose.
